subject.title: Feature: Global session reset on auth switch

question: Should OpenClaw expose an admin-scoped global auth refresh that preserves session context, and if so what authority, active-run, and per-session failure semantics must it guarantee?
rationale: The feature affects every active session and credential-routing boundary; source evidence does not establish a safe default for authorization or lifecycle behavior.

options.title: Sponsor a scoped auth-refresh API
options.body: Define an additive admin-only gateway capability that preserves canonical session context while refreshing only auth-backed bindings and reports per-session outcomes.

options.title: Keep auth refresh session-scoped
options.body: Retain the existing keyed reset model and document that provider or credential changes require deliberate per-session recovery.

options.title: Design the broader reconcile surface first
options.body: Align this request with the open model/session-override reconciliation work before committing to a separate global lifecycle API.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a scoped auth-refresh API
recommendation.body: Define an additive admin-only gateway capability that preserves canonical session context while refreshing only auth-backed bindings and reports per-session outcomes.

likelyOwner.reason: The recorded discussion and recent gateway/session lifecycle history make this person the strongest routing candidate for the API and security-boundary decision.
